item.title: Short-Term vs Long-Term Memory in Agentic AI
item.description:
Short-term and long-term memory in agentic AI differ by scope. Short-term memory is the agent’s state for one task: messages, tool results, the plan. It lives in the prompt and ends with the thread. Long-term memory lives in an external store, survives across sessions, and is retrieved selectively. Agents need both, plus a path that moves information between them.

This page compares the two side by side and shows how they connect in code. Each type has its own deep dive: short-term memory in AI agents and AI agent long-term memory. The pillar, AI agent memory explained, covers the full taxonomy.

item.title: AI Agent Long-Term Memory: How It Works, How to Build It
item.description:
AI agent long-term memory is information an agent keeps across sessions: facts about users, past events, and lessons from earlier tasks. The model can’t hold it, because LLMs forget each conversation when the call ends. So the agent’s code writes memories to an external store and, on each new turn, retrieves the few that matter into the prompt.

Building it well comes down to a handful of design choices: what to store, how to index it, how to search it, and how the model reads what comes back. This page walks through each, using findings from the LongMemEval benchmark, then shows a working example. The pillar guide, AI agent memory explained, covers memory types and tools in more breadth.
